C.B. entered the washroom under the pretext of assisting C.M.A. with hygiene.
C.B. told both, C.M.A. and C.D.A., not to tell their mother what he had done.
They both testified to being afraid that their brother would hit them if they told their mother.
C.B. had hit C.M.A. on at least one occasion in front of witnesses.

crime_highlights: Mr. Carter immediately turned on the headlights of the van and fired at Mr. Whiteside with his own firearm.
Mr. Whiteside was struck in the head and in the leg by two of Mr. Carter's bullets. As I noted earlier, he died almost instantly.
A bullet fired by Mr. Carter penetrated the back passenger side door and struck Alfred Wong in the right side of his chest, puncturing his stomach and proceeding through to his heart.
Alfred Wong died two days later.
rationale_highlights: The IRCA report does describe some race and cultural factors that, I agree, may have affected Mr. Carter's decision-making and contributed to poor choices.
He also felt that he was treated differently because of his race
In assessing Mr. Carter's degree of responsibility for the offences I take into account the racism Mr. Carter experienced as a Black person.
Mr. Carter's degree of responsibility for the offences is nonetheless high.
note: Court accepts racism as relevant but finds responsibility still high.
